*Policy: PHP & Moodle supported versions*

Since Moodle 3.5 ([MDL-59159|https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-59159]), these rules apply to decide the Minimum PHP and Moodle versions supported:

# An LTS will always require the previous LTS (or later) for upgrading.
# The maximum PHP version supported for a branch will be the maximum one achieved throughout the life of the branch. Usually with .0 releases, but it may happen later (we added support for php70 with 3.0.1 or support for php73 with 3.6.4, for example).
# The minimum PHP version supported for a branch will be *the lower of*:
#* The [minimum version supported in any way by php|http://php.net/supported-versions.php] that is under support for at least 12 more months when the new Moodle version gets released (so we provide slow, progressive increments).
#* The maximum PHP version supported by the previous LTS branch (so we guarantee jumping between LTS is possible without upgrading PHP at the same time).
{panel}

We need to decide ASAP about all the PHP/DB/Moodle version requirements and put all of them into the environmental tests (adding them to all supported branches).

All the still open linked issues have also been cloned here from the 5.1 sister issue (MDL-85362).

fields.summary: Make the autocomplete form element more accessible

issuetype.description: A problem which impairs or prevents Moodle from functioning correctly. (Migrated on 14 Jun 2025 12:11 UTC)
issuetype.name: Bug

fields.description:
There are several items that we can do to improve the accessibility of the autocomplete form element. Please see below:

# This issue was identified in the recent accessibility audit for LMS and Workplace, where assistive technology users, such as screen reader users, are unaware that the selected items on the autocomplete element can be deleted by pressing Enter or Space. There’s only an {{X}} icon that visually indicates that selected items can be deleted, but this is not obvious for users who are blind or have low vision. This fails the Level AAA Success Criterion 1.3.6 Identify Purpose.
# The Axe DevTools extension flags the following issues on the autocomplete element:
## When there are no selected items, an invalid ARIA attribute value is raised for the aria-activedescendant attribute. For example:
### {noformat}Invalid ARIA attribute value: aria-activedescendant="form_autocomplete_selection-1760326862721-NaN"{noformat}

## Another issue involves the autocomplete selection container, which has a {{listbox}} role, when it does not have selected items.
### {noformat}Ensure elements with an ARIA role that require child roles contain them

<div class="form-autocomplete-selection w-100 form-autocomplete-multiple" id="form_autocomplete_selection-1760326862721" aria-labelledby="form_autocomplete_selection-1760326862721-label" role="listbox" aria-atomic="true" tabindex="0" aria-multiselectable="true" aria-activedescendant="form_autocomplete_selection-1760326862721-NaN" data-active-value="a">

To solve this problem, you need to fix the following:
Required ARIA children role not present: group, option{noformat}

# The first item on the selections list also has a focus outline, which can confuse users, thinking that the page’s focus is currently on the selection, when it’s really not.
## For example, in the screenshot below, the focus is actually on the “Course full name” field, but the selected course category shows a focus outline. We must display the focus outline only when the selected item is really in focus.
!image-20251015-024118.png|width=839,height=356,alt="image-20251015-024118.png"!

fields.description:
The most common complaint we get almost every time a pentest is done is when too many people have an xss risk and its quite tedious to track these down at the moment.

fields.description:
As part of the Open Telemetry work, we should investigate how best to create a new Moodle {{logstore}} plugin.

This will likely need to use a PSR-3 logger implementation, such as Monolog. Alternatively we may be better advised to create a new {{\core\logger}} API which the {{moodle-logstore_otel}} calls to log data.

The creation of this related API is a part of _this_ issue.

We should be careful not to have scope creep here. If we do use Monolog (hint, we will be using Monolog), we only want it logging Moodle Logstore events in the first instance. We are not looking at {{mtrace}}, or {{debugging}} messages. These are a totally separate problem space, which arguably needs much better definition and are discussed in [https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-50592|https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-50592|smart-link].

I have already created an Open Telemetry Logstore plugin as part of the proof-of-concept, but parts of this are from [https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-50592|https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-50592|smart-link] and may include scope creep.

The changes that I’ve written:

* may need stripping back a little
* need tests
* needs to be compatible with the logging implementation in MoodleCloud

The {{\core\logger}} API:

* should have _minimal_ dependencies such that it can be used in early stages of the Moodle bootstrap
* should not error if the dependenices that are present (that is Monolog) are missing from disk (for example, if the {{composer install}} has not yet taken place)
* should be loaded using the Dependency Injector
* should support [PSR-3|https://www.php-fig.org/psr/psr-3/] channels

fields.description:
Hello!

Chrome 142 turned on restrictions about public servers accessing things on the local network: [https://developer.chrome.com/blog/local-network-access|https://developer.chrome.com/blog/local-network-access|smart-link] 

For use this broke the LTI for Turn It In, when Launch container = Embed. This shouldn’t be specific to Turn It In though, any embedded LTI that authenticates with a Moodle server with a private IP address will fail on Chrome 142 and later. The iframe loads these URLs:

# {{https://moodle-server/mod/lti/launch.php?id=4&triggerview=0}}
# {{https://lti.int.turnitin.com/oidc/login/xxx}}
# {{https://moodle-server/mod/lti/auth.php}} (fails with LocalNetworkAccessPermissionDenied)

Our {{moodle-server}} has split-horizon DNS, on campus users get a 10.x.x.x IP, Internet users get a public IP. [lti.int.turnitin.com|http://lti.int.turnitin.com] has public IPs.

I added “local-network-access *” in mod/lti/view.php where it builds the <iframe allow="">attribute. Now Chrome prompts for local network access permissions and then loads the LTI. Other LTIs that don’t redirect back don’t prompt for local network access.

It feels Chrome is wrong, but the sane fix is in Moodle.  And the only fix is in Moodle code. Or changing our network.

Thanks!

*Replication steps:*
Run a Moodle instance on localhost or a private IP. Add an LTI activity hosted on a public IP. The LTI has to authenticate back to the original Moodle. Chrome 142 will display an error instead of showing the LTI:

“The connection is blocked because it was initiated by a public page to connect to devices or servers on your private network. Reload this page to allow the connection.”

Reloading the page doesn’t work.

This button must link the user directly back to the main course page from which the activity was launched.

h3. (/) *Acceptance criteria*
